text: The step builds against the plan's H row and records the four rows the build also needs — the rwb-case case list and case-move answer, the rwb-source-data COLLINS score and the rwb-decision package read — as consumed contract rows with their placeholders rather than adding them to the metadata.
why: The plan fixes the H, C, I and X rows of every slice and a worker may not rewrite them, yet the step cannot run without those rows and evaluates a rule package that the plan's pattern set does not declare.
read: The four rows are named in 12.2, faked in 12.8 and marked class C in the text; DP-04 and DP-05 are recorded as absent rows, the package is read as data on the owner's read, and REQ-S6-001 is traced from the FSD Requirements served table.
confirm: Solution architect and the owners of rwb-case, rwb-source-data and rwb-decision
impact: The story can start on Day 1; the dependency map under-reports four rows and the absent DP-04 row until it is corrected

text: This step publishes no event and consumes no event; the service's topic and its two events are the award and transfer stories', and the outbox library is recorded as the absent platform row of the topic rather than added to the H row.
why: Architecture v5 gives rwb-debtsale the topic with LotAwarded and AccountsTransferred while the selection awards nothing and transfers nothing, and the plan's pattern set omits DP-09.
read: Sections 12.3 and 12.4 are None, outbox_event sits in the schema as a library object with no row written here, and RWB-PLT-TE006-CON is named as the wave 0 library the service's topic needs.
confirm: Platform library owner and the owners of rwb-case and rwb-payment
impact: No event is declared or built at this step, and the absence test refuses one; the later publishing stories still need the library row

text: The FSD S6 Debt sale v3 and the TSD S6 Debt sale v2 module files stand in for the absent S6 extract and are the source text of this step.
why: The run's extract folder holds no S6 extract, and the module files sit above any summary in the precedence order.
read: Every value of sections 2 to 18 is taken from the FSD S6 v3, the TSD S6 v2, the Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 or the legacy story, and section 18 names the two module files as the source text.
confirm: Business analyst
impact: No value is taken from a summary or a deck; the extract folder is corrected in a later run

text: The 54 percent cap is carried by R-DS-19 and its criterion and test are RWB-S6-E6005-APP's; this story reads the cap value from the package, records it with the version and proves the eligibility selection only.
why: Legacy AC1 names the cap in the eligibility step, while R-DS-01 carries no cap condition and the only cap row of the route set is R-DS-19 at the bidding close.
read: The legacy words of AC1 are kept unchanged, the cap appears as a rule fact in the decision record and in BR6, R-DS-19 is tabled out of this story in section 8, and section 18 names it as RWB-S6-E6005-APP's.
confirm: Business analyst and the owner of RWB-S6-E6005-APP
impact: No cap threshold is written in this build, and the cap outcome is proved where the award is tested

text: The eligibility inputs deviation_open and fraud_flag are carried as consumed rule inputs of the rwb-case case row and the score data product, with their field names and owner left as the placeholder until an owner publishes them.
why: R-DS-01 and R-DS-02 test the two facts, and neither the S6 field list nor the case field list of the legacy Data table nor the Ownership Map names a field or an owner for them.
read: The rows of 12.2 declare the inputs as part of the consumed case and score rows and the fakes answer them; section 11 and section 19 record them as Not specified in the source documents.
confirm: Solution architect and the owners of rwb-case, rwb-source-data and rwb-deviation
impact: The step is buildable and testable on the fakes; the field names are confirmed before the contract is tagged

text: The lot build and price step builds against the plan's H row and treats the rwb-source-data, rwb-agent, rwb-case and rwb-decision rows as class C dependencies it records in the text and fakes, without adding them to the metadata.
why: The plan fixes the H, C, I and X rows of every slice and a worker may not rewrite them, yet the step cannot run without the COLLINS economics, the agent estimate, the case state and the package in force.
read: The five consumed rows are declared in section 12.2 with their owners and placeholders, faked in section 12.8, and named in the dependency text of section 13; the case move is read as the workflow stage outcome; the DP-04 and DP-09 rows stay in this register.
confirm: Solution architect and the owners of rwb-source-data, rwb-agent, rwb-case and rwb-decision
impact: The story starts on Day 1 against fakes and the dependency map under-reports four rows until it is corrected

text: The price estimate is the pricing agent of rwb-agent, consumed on its contract with a 60 s budget and the rule fallback, and DP-20 is recorded as an absent pattern row rather than added.
why: The legacy feature names a model gateway and the kit routes the estimate through the pricing agent under R-UNI-32, while the plan's pattern set for this key carries DP03, DP13 and DP19 only and no source publishes the agent operation.
read: The run is declared as consumed from P10 rwb-agent with the estimate per lot and per account, the confidence and the schema-check verdict, one hop, and the rule answer is used after 60 s; the client dependencies RWB-PLT-TE013-CON and RWB-P10-TE013-CON are named in section 13.
confirm: Solution architect and the rwb-agent owner
impact: No model, prompt or agent table is built in rwb-debtsale and the estimate is reached on the owner's contract

text: The COLLINS score and lot economics are read only on the rwb-source-data data product with its as-of date, and no v_ace_score view and no ACE table is read by rwb-debtsale.
why: The legacy feature reads recovery.v_ace_score and the FSD names the view, while Architecture v5 gives the 30 v_ace_* views to rwb-source-data alone and rwb-debtsale holds no view grant.
read: The data product is declared as a consumed row with its freshness stamp and its operation name placeholder; the field IDs of the data product are left missing; the boundary test fails a build that reads a view or another schema.
confirm: Solution architect and the rwb-source-data owner
impact: No ACE grant is requested for rwb-debtsale and the lot is built from the data product

text: The FSD S6 Debt sale v3 and the TSD S6 Debt sale v2 module files stand in for the missing S6 extract and are read directly.
why: Fill order R7.3 names the FSD and TSD module files, the work package expects extracts of them in _work/msr/extract, and that folder holds no S6 file.
read: Every FSD and TSD value of this story is taken from the module files themselves and no value is taken from a summary; the extract gap is documentation only and changes no value.
confirm: Business analyst who owns the extract set
impact: The story is complete without the extract; the run's extract set gains the S6 files at the next pass

text: R-DS-04 is tabled in this story and its criterion stays with RWB-S6-E6001-APP AC3, so this story proves the priced lot and the LOT_WITH_COMMITTEE answer and claims no criterion of the rule.
why: The rule produces the priced lot here but its proposal becomes binding at the committee, and the plan gives the committee story four criteria of its own.
read: The rule row is copied character for character in section 8; the state it produces, the fields reserve_price, payment_terms, buyer_class and selling_price and the case-move answer are proved here; the criterion is named as RWB-S6-E6001-APP AC3's in sections 7, 8 and 18.
confirm: Business analyst and the owner of RWB-S6-E6001-APP
impact: No criterion is owned twice and the committee story owns the approval and the binding terms

text: The minimum lot size, the reserve and selling-price basis, the payment-terms ladder and the buyer-class rule are versioned reference data or rule rows whose values no source gives, and the priced state of SCR-25 is carried by the decision record and the case route state rather than by a lot status.
why: FSD S6 BR-S6-002 requires every changeable value to be reference data with a version, no source states these four values, and LOV-LOT-STATUS has no PRICED value although the legacy screen declares a priced state.
read: The values are read with their version and left missing where no source gives them; the lot stays BUILDING until the committee sets OFFERED; the priced state is a decision-record fact and a case route state.
confirm: Business analyst, the product owner and the rwb-decision owner
impact: No business value is written in code and the screen shows a priced state that the data model carries

text: The data-room slice builds against the plan's H row and records the three consumed rows it also needs as facts rather than adding them to the metadata.
why: The plan fixes the H, C, I and X rows of every slice; a worker may not rewrite them, yet the step cannot run without the rwb-document tape, the rwb-partner panel and the rwb-case state and move answer.
read: The rwb-document tape read, the rwb-partner panel read and the rwb-case state read and move answer are named in the text, faked for the build and recorded as missing rows; REQ-S6-003 is traced from the program and the FSD while the plan carries no requirement id.
confirm: Solution architect and the owners of rwb-document, rwb-partner and rwb-case
impact: The story starts on Day 1 against the three fakes; the dependency map under-reports three rows until it is corrected

text: The data-room read is one Partner portal operation of rwb-debtsale reached by the buyer through the partner gateway in the DMZ and the rwb-partner panel, with PT-BUYER RU scoped to its own cases, and the staff roles of the legacy row keep Partner portal R through the Workbench.
why: API-S6-004 is S6's in the Ownership Map while the legacy permission row names staff roles and TSD S6 T6.1 names PT-BUYER; no plan row covers the partner channel and DP-19 names only the gateway-bff composite route.
read: The route of the read is the partner gateway and the rwb-partner panel, the panel facts arrive on the rwb-partner contract with the placeholder on the operation name, PRT-05 is the buyer panel of rwb-partner, and the two right statements are kept as one declaration of the operation.
confirm: Solution architect, the edge story owner and the rwb-partner owner
impact: The read is built and faked on Day 1 and the partner entry is declared rather than built; the edge and partner rows are added to the dependency map

text: The masked tape is read back on the rwb-document contract and only its reference and its masking-check outcome are carried; the building, the masking, the rejection and the rebuild stay with RWB-S6-E5025-APP, the PII service and the policy of rwb-access.
why: R-DS-10 to R-DS-12 are the tape path of the sibling slice and no source publishes a tape object, operation or masking rule catalogue of this module.
read: The tape read is one consumed row of P5 with the placeholder on its operation name; the story stores no tape row, applies no mask and relaxes none, and the no-personal-data test covers the account element of the answer.
confirm: Solution architect and the rwb-document owner
impact: No tape is rebuilt and no masking rule is copied into rwb-debtsale; the room can only open on a tape the sibling story produced and masked

text: The legacy FSD S6 Debt sale v3 and TSD S6 Debt sale v2 files stand in for the module extract, because the extract folder holds no S6 extract.
why: The WP's read-only list names the S6 extract files and none exists, while the module text is needed for the rule rows, the columns, the lists and the operation detail.
read: The module values are taken from the legacy FSD S6 v3 and TSD S6 v2 under aisdlc/requirement/legacy, with the R7.3 fill order unchanged, and every quotation is the legacy module wording.
confirm: Business analyst and the extract set owner
impact: The story is complete against the module files; a later S6 extract must be diffed before the contract baseline is tagged

text: The data room is the read answer over debt_sale_lot, debt_sale_account and the P5 tape with no table of its own, the lot status after the opening is OFFERED of LOV-LOT-STATUS, and the lot properties the partner read withholds are settled in the contract baseline review.
why: Architecture v5 names a data room in the schema and TSD S6 T3.1 defines no such table, LOV-LOT-STATUS has no DATA_ROOM_OPEN value, and no source states the field set the partner sees before the award.
read: No table, no column and no migration are added; the opening writes the lot status and its standard columns only, and the withheld properties carry the placeholder until the baseline review.
confirm: Solution architect and the data steward
impact: The room is a read projection and the lot carries one status change; a source that names a data-room table or a withheld field set would amend the contract, not the schema

text: The approval step builds against the plan's H row and against the published rwb-decision, rwb-access and rwb-case documents and fakes, and records the five rows the build also needs as facts rather than adding them to the metadata.
why: The plan fixes the H, C, I and X rows of every slice and a worker may not rewrite them, yet the step cannot run without the P7 approval chain and rule package, the P4 DoA limit and the P3 state read and move answer; two of those rows have no published operation name.
read: The five consumed rows are named in the text and in 12.2, faked for the build, and recorded as missing C rows; the rule-package read and the case-move answer carry the placeholder 'Not specified in the source documents' until their owners publish a name.
confirm: Solution architect and the owners of rwb-decision, rwb-access and rwb-case
impact: The story can start on Day 1; the dependency map under-reports five C rows and one Temporal queue dependency until it is corrected

text: The committee approval is P7's child ApprovalWorkflow of the kit, started by this step on the rwb-decision queue, and this story reads its answer and writes no approval row and no ledger entry.
why: Architecture v5 and the Temporal design give the approval to rwb-decision as a kit child workflow, while the FSD and the legacy story read as if the step approved and logged in one process; the sources also name the act once in the architecture slide and three times in the Ownership Map.
read: The act is the Ownership Map's POST /approvals/{approvalId}/approve, /return and /refuse, read as the arch slide's POST /approvals/{id}/decide; the chain is correlated by a record this story holds, and the DoA lookup is passed to it as a parameter.
confirm: rwb-decision owner and the solution architect
impact: No approval table is created in rwb_debtsale and the child-workflow input and return signal are confirmed before the contract is tagged

text: The story is stated in wave 4 with release 30 April 2027 as the plan and the legacy epic give it, and the wave 3 creation of the service is recorded rather than resolved.
why: EP06 is wave 4 in the W-MAP and the legacy epic carries 30 April 2027, while Architecture v5 creates rwb-debtsale in wave 3; R5.6 only keeps the W-MAP wave when it is earlier than the service wave, so the case is not covered by the rule.
read: The plan's wave and release values are copied unchanged and the release is marked tentative; the service creates in wave 3 and this key delivers in wave 4 alongside the other EP06 keys.
confirm: Solution architect and the wave planner
impact: One service delivers in two waves with two releases, and the wave map needs the statement before the build order is fixed

text: The award operation API-S6-003 and the A right of the legacy table belong to RWB-S6-E6005-APP, and the committee act is an approval-chain answer under the P4 DoA limit rather than a Workbench right.
why: The legacy key rows both endpoints and the A right, the target split gives the award its own story, and the FSD's committee role has no row in the T6.1 matrix.
read: This story provides the lot read with right R and writes the approval columns; API-S6-003, its AwardRequest, its DecisionLogEntry answer and the buyer columns are named as RWB-S6-E6005-APP's, and approval_authority is written from the approval's answer.
confirm: Solution architect and the owner of the award story
impact: No award operation is declared or built here and the authority of the approval is carried as a lot column, so no right is invented for the committee

text: FSD S6 Debt sale v3 and TSD S6 Debt sale v2 are read directly from the requirements folders as the module pair the extract would have carried, and the fill order of R7.3 is unchanged.
why: The Work Package asks for S6 extract files and the extract folder holds none, while both module documents exist and are the sources of the field catalog, the lists, the rules, the messages and the endpoints.
read: The FSD and TSD module documents are the second and third sources of the fill order for every S6 story of this Work Package, and no other extract is substituted for them.
confirm: Run lead
impact: Every S6 story is filled from the same two documents and the extract gap is documentation only

text: The lot takes payment_terms and status from TSD S6 T3.1, the approval is a case route state and not a lot status, and REQ-S6-002 is the requirement the step traces to.
why: The FSD field catalog omits payment_terms and status although the rule approves the tiered terms, LOV-LOT-STATUS has no value for an approved lot, and the requirement mapping of FEAT-DBS-05 differs between the FSD and the TSD.
read: DF-SAL-027, DF-SAL-028 and DF-SAL-029 are written and DF-SAL-030 is read only; the lot stays BUILDING at approval and the route state LOT_APPROVED stays on the case of record; REQ-S6-002 is cited with the mapping difference recorded.
confirm: Solution architect, the FSD owner and the TSD owner
impact: The tiered terms have a field to live in, the lot status vocabulary is not stretched, and the traceability row states the requirement without inventing a mapping

text: The qualification slice builds against the plan's H row, records the four consumed contracts and the authorise call as class C rows in the text and the registers, and keeps the metadata C row as the plan states it.
why: The plan fixes the H, C, I and X rows of every slice and a worker may not rewrite them, yet the step cannot run without the rwb-partner buyer facts, the rwb-case state and move answer, the rwb-decision package and the rwb-access right.
read: The rwb-partner buyer panel read, the rwb-case state read and move answer, the rwb-decision package read and the rwb-access authorise call are named in the text, faked for the build and recorded as missing rows; REQ-S6-004 is read from the FSD requirements table and the program BRD.
confirm: Solution architect and the owners of rwb-partner, rwb-case, rwb-access and rwb-decision
impact: The story can start on Day 1; the dependency map under-reports five rows until it is corrected

text: This story provides no REST operation of its own: the qualification step runs behind the award operation API-S6-003 and the data room read API-S6-004, which are sibling stories', and behind the bid operation API-S6-005.
why: TSD S6 appendix T-A publishes no KYC or qualification operation and the two endpoint rows of the legacy story belong to RWB-S6-E6005-APP and RWB-S6-E5026-APP, so declaring either as this story's own would duplicate a sibling's operation.
read: The step is triggered by the access request on API-S6-004 and the bid on API-S6-005; the qualification element is fixed as an embedded element of the answers those operations publish, and the two legacy endpoint rows are named by owner in the text.
confirm: Solution architect and the owners of the award and data room stories
impact: No operation is duplicated between three stories of the same service; a later T-A version may add a qualification read

text: The partner channel reads the same qualification element through the partner gateway in the DMZ and the staff screens read it through the gateway-bff composite route, and neither channel is built here.
why: TSD S6 T6.1 gives PT-BUYER a scoped RU right and Architecture v5 puts a partner gateway in front of rwb-partner, while no story, platform row or X row of this slice owns that channel.
read: The element is served read only on the service base and reached behind the two gateways; the partner channel and the gateway are recorded as a missing row and stubbed by a partner gateway fake.
confirm: Solution architect and the edge owner
impact: The internal build is unaffected and the partner read is testable on a fake until the edge row exists

text: The story keeps the EP06 wave 4 while rwb-debtsale is created in wave 3, and the qualification step builds on Day 1 against its contract baseline.
why: Template and Rules R5.6 keeps the later W-MAP wave and raises one conflict gap per service and business epic.
read: Wave 4 stands on the story and the CON story is Day 1; the difference is recorded once for S6 and EP06 and the release date stays 30 April 2027 (tentative).
confirm: Delivery lead
impact: Sequencing is unchanged and the story is not re-planned into wave 3

text: The legacy FSD S6 Debt sale v3 and TSD S6 Debt sale v2 files are read as the module sources because the extract folder holds no S6 module text.
why: The fill order of R7.3 needs the FSD and TSD module files, the WP points at the S6 extract which does not exist, and the two legacy files are the same documents in their source folder.
read: Every value of the story comes from the legacy story, those two module files, the Business Rules and Routing Logic workbook and the Architecture v5 extract; the substitution is recorded once.
confirm: Business analyst
impact: The story is complete and traceable; the extract set has to be reconciled with it later

text: The bid is recorded on the existing lot columns and the account set of the lot, while the bid amount, its time and its reference stay in the decision record until a bid column set exists.
why: R-DS-18 records a bid against the lot and the buyer and Architecture v5 gives S6 'bids', but TSD S6 T3.1 declares no bid column on debt_sale_lot or debt_sale_account and this story may not add one.
read: buyer_partner_id, buyer_class and status are written on debt_sale_lot, the bid is bound to the debt_sale_account rows of the lot, and the amount and the window are carried by the decision record and the screen answer.
confirm: Data steward and the DB story owner of this service
impact: The bid is recorded and testable on Day 1; the award story needs the column set before it reads an amount

text: The FSD S6 Debt sale v3 and TSD S6 Debt sale v2 module documents stand in for the extract files the Work Package names, and the R7.3 fill order is applied unchanged.
why: The Work Package points at extract files that do not exist, and no story of this Work Package can be filled without the FSD and TSD module pair; the two documents are the highest available sources after the legacy story.
read: The FSD S6 v3 sections A2.1 to A2.7 and the TSD S6 v2 T2 to T6.1 and T-A are read directly from the requirements folders and cited as FSD S6 and TSD S6.
applied_in: Every story of WP B-S6-01, sections 2, 3, 8, 11 and 14
confirm: Run lead and the extract step
impact: No value is invented and the citations stay resolvable; the extract set is one module pair short until it is rebuilt

text: The plan's wave, release and dependency rows stand as written: a step that needs a fact from a sibling slice of the same service consumes it on that owner's contract and names the sibling story in section 19 instead of adding a build row.
why: The plan fixes the metadata of every slice and a worker may not rewrite it, while the tape, award and transfer slices of rwb-debtsale are delivered by other Work Packages and the two EP06 keys keep the later W-MAP wave inside a wave 3 service.
read: The masked tape is RWB-S6-E5025-APP's, LotAwarded is RWB-S6-E6005-APP's, AccountsTransferred is RWB-S6-E6007-APP's; the data-room step reads the tape on the rwb-document contract and every step answers the case move to rwb-case.
confirm: Solution architect and the owners of the sibling slices
impact: No dependency row is changed and no release date is moved; the slice boundaries are recorded so the wave 3 and wave 4 harnesses know which story builds which step
